summary_hint: Tells a processor which trust document this is, which trust, who the current trustees are, and whether they may borrow and encumber.

typed_core.why: identity/disambiguator — certification vs amendment vs restatement drives what it proves (degraded from enum)

typed_core.name: trust_name
typed_core.why: identity — the trust the loan vests into

typed_core.name: document_execution_date
typed_core.why: recency — when this instrument was executed; which version is operative

typed_core.why: processor — the event that elevates a successor trustee

typed_core.why: processor — revocable vs irrevocable headline (degraded from enum)

fields.name: signature_present

encoding_variations: Subtype varies: 'Certification of Trust', 'Certificate of Trust', 'First Amendment to…', 'Amended and Restated…' — trust_document_subtype beside document_title disambiguates what the instrument proves

A certification abstracts the full trust: it asserts powers (borrow/mortgage) rather than granting them — capture the asserted authority flags with certification_current_and_unamended beside them, since a certification's value depends on it being current
Original trust date vs this document's execution date frequently differ (an amendment years later) — both anchor the correct trust and version
Successor-trustee triggers stated as events (death/incapacity/resignation) — capture verbatim

open_questions.q: Which repeating list to keep. Chose authorized_signer_names_and_capacity (who may sign the mortgage) over property_or_asset_references.
open_questions.recommendation: authorized_signer_names_and_capacity is the higher-value list; if asset/property linkage is needed, flag whether a second list is warranted (exceeds the one-list budget) GEET'S DECISION (LP-438): BUILD IT — LP-437 made nested lists cheap (one declaration + the generic mechanism); the one-list-budget / defer / no-consumer concern is overturned. Build as flat_row; the per-rule consumer is separate follow-up.

open_questions.q: Certification vs full agreement overlap. This type overlaps packet 099.
open_questions.recommendation: keep both distinct — a certification asserts, an agreement grants; note the classifier must reliably separate them

open_questions.q: Authority flags degraded to str, null-when-silent. No bool coercer.
open_questions.recommendation: confirm downstream distinguishes null from 'No', and that a certification's asserted authority is treated as weaker evidence than the agreement's granting clause

notes: This is often a Certification of Trust — an abstract that asserts trustee authority — distinct from the full agreement (packet 099); the authority flags reflect what is certified, not the granting clause.
Capture the current trustees and the authorized signers separately (a signer may act under a power of attorney or as co-trustee).
Record authority flags null when silent; do not infer.

No PII requiring registration — a certification/amendment typically omits the trust TIN; if a given instrument prints the trust TIN, register it as in packet 099 (tax_identification_number_masked, pre_masked true).
Ambiguity: document_execution_date is tagged 'recency' (not one of the five reason classes); mapped to reason_class 'processor' (freshness/which-version-is-operative is a processor-facing concern).
